api.acquire: acquire(&AppHandle, opaqueOwner:String, documentEpoch:u64, Validity, OnAcquired, OnLost) -> Result<Grant,AcquireError>; AcquireError contains message and optional retained_grant for an explicitly failed rollback, never a false success
api.release: release(&AppHandle, Grant) -> Result<bool,String>; false is stale/duplicate and cannot mutate the window
api.isCurrent: is_current(&AppHandle,&Grant) -> bool; read-only exact identity check for caller reconciliation
api.grant: Serializable owner/documentEpoch/revision/windowKey; windowKey is a random incarnation capability, not a raw native handle. No media/channel/account identity.
api.callbacks: Validity is Arc<dyn Fn()->bool+Send+Sync>; OnAcquired and OnLost are Arc<dyn Fn(Grant)+Send+Sync>. Both notification callbacks execute inside the serialized main-thread operation, outside the coordinator mutex. Native caller commits its exact local grant in OnAcquired, not after acquire returns; this prevents acquire A response from restoring A after B superseded it. OnLost clears only that exact grant. Caller captures weak lifecycle and exact epoch and never holds a domain/grant mutex while calling acquire/release. Mutation from callbacks is rejected; read-only is_current is allowed.

serialization: Main-thread calls are detected with GetWindowThreadProcessId(main HWND)==GetCurrentThreadId and execute inline; they never queue and wait for themselves. Other callers dispatch one bounded queue ticket to the main thread.

Queued wait is2seconds. Pending ticket atomically becomes Cancelled on timeout, so a later queue callback performs no mutation. If the callback already atomically became Running, wait for its actual completion rather than returning an ordinary timeout followed by a late grant. Root explicitly approved this truthful distinction; the native OS call has no claimed hard runtime bound. Window-handle resolution is also an existing Tauri synchronous getter, not claimed cancellable.

A per-coordinator main-thread reentrancy guard rejects nested mutation. Owner mutex is not held across validity, native fullscreen mutation/readback or callbacks. Commit only after successful native state readback, retaining old owner on native failure.

Validate provider intent immediately before native enter, after the native operation, and after the serialized OnAcquired callback. A close racing the callback either observes its installed grant or is caught by the final validity check. Internal revocation releases only that exact new grant. If rollback/exit fails, retain retryable ownership and return an explicit AcquireError with retained_grant; notify no false OnLost. A failed new acquisition does not give the caller a different previous owner's grant. No synchronous OS-call or callback hard runtime bound is claimed.

Supersession enters/retains fullscreen without an intermediate exit, commits the newer revision, then invokes old weak onLost outside the owner mutex. A stale old release is a no-op. Same exact owner+epoch+window acquisition is idempotent.

Window destroyed invalidates its random incarnation and clears only that incarnation's owner. A recreated main window gets a new key even if Windows reuses its HWND. Window-lifecycle callbacks cannot release another incarnation's owner.
